extracted.intended_audience: travelers and general readers (especially Americans) interested in experiencing Rome/Italy
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative criteria for visiting and understanding Rome (and for travel writing about it): how long to stay, how to see the city, how to interpret its rites and people, and how to behave respectfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the 'nine-days wonder' approach to Rome
rubrics_metrics.description: Rome is not a nine-days wonder; those who try to make it such lose the ideal Rome (and gain no true knowledge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to 'see Rome' in a brief whirlwind tour. Short, rushed sight‑seeing yields only impressions of hues and outlines, not the real knowledge or assimilation of Rome's soul. Stay longer (weeks rather than days) to gain true appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live and walk daily to know the city
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than going out each day only to 'see a sight', live in Rome and walk every day; familiarity reveals Ancient and Modern Rome in distinct ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make everyday walks part of your stay so you encounter objects of interest organically; use long evenings for reflection and follow-up study. Familiarity allows superstructures to 'vanish' and the local habitation of thoughts to appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare by studying history and literature to interpret rites and imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: To understand the legends, rites, and rich tapestry of Rome (which can appear as a 'senseless mass of juggleries' to the uninformed), one must consult books and historical references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring or read relevant histories and literature so that paintings, chapels, and ceremonial practices have coherent, poetic meaning rather than seeming merely picturesque or absurd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time for assimilation when viewing art and monuments
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeing great works (like the Venus, Domenichino frescos, or the recumbent St. Cecilia) requires time; a hurried glance cannot produce true appreciation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spend sustained, quiet time with works that move you; avoid the fatigue and confusion of rapid sight‑seeing that prevents the mind from receiving and integrating aesthetic impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe respectful conduct at religious ceremonies and cemeteries
rubrics_metrics.description: Religious observances and cemetery rites in Rome are meaningful; outsiders should not violate ceremonies or treat them as mere curiosities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be reverent and attentive in chapels and processions (note the chanting boys, praying people, wax groups). Do not treat ceremonies as entertainment—avoid disruptive behavior or flippant comments ascribed to insensitive sightseers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect local etiquette and political sensitivities in public displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Public demonstrations and symbols (e.g., flags) can be subject to local ordinances and political concerns; heed these limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before displaying political emblems or staging demonstrations, be aware of local rules and the potential for provocation; what seems a patriotic gesture at home may be restricted or inflammatory abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge nations and societies by moral and democratic criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating countries, look for 'genuine democracy', 'child-like wisdom' in learning, aversion to falsehood, and the real-hearted love and achievements that benefit all men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use substantive moral measures—degree of rights respected, charity, public virtue—rather than surface wealth or talent alone. Public failures (wealth with cruel poverty, conventional life) indicate shortcomings despite long cultural histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate political/religious leaders by generosity of heart and moral influence
rubrics_metrics.description: A leader's real power and worth are shown by a generous human heart, sympathy, and moral example (the Pope is praised for a 'generous human heart' that attracts and consoles the people).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing rulers or spiritual heads, prioritize their humane impulses, personal charity, and capacity to inspire over mere pomp or political posturing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity as a virtue in travel writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed words have merit when sincere; yielding to one's feelings in writing about a place confers value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow genuine feeling and honest impressions to shape travel accounts. Authentic, heartfelt description is itself a sign of quality in literary reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with local popular culture and performances to understand character
rubrics_metrics.description: Attending local dances, balls, and festivals (e.g., the Saltarello, civic balls) reveals national spirit and individuality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe and study popular performances and public gatherings—they often provide revealing moments of 'natural poetry' and communal tact that communicate a people's character better than formal sights alone.
